# Sprint 1: managed storefront candidate

Base: `snapshot/quickshell-20261012` (404c021), paired with the
`sprint1/storefronts` branches of `citrineio/zaman-menu` and `citrineio/dukkan`.
The recovery acceptance round passed on Kadhem's Q6A on 2026-10-14.
Device builds and activation were performed by the owner. Local Python/JS
checks alone do not establish Rust/Qt compilation or device acceptance.
See `sprint1-acceptance-20261014.md` for the exact tested scope and deferred work.

## Session contract

- Pegasus stays tiled and borderless in `library`.
- Each managed storefront runs as its own transient user service:
  `zaman-store-dukkan.service`, `zaman-store-steam.service`.
- Descendant windows are matched by PID/cgroup, including Xwayland; they are
  placed in `store-dukkan`/`store-steam`, with Dukkan fullscreen. Steam retains its own window/fullscreen policy.
- The resident layer-shell menu does not disable storefront fullscreen.
- Home hides the storefront workspace while preserving its process. Reopening
  Storefronts resumes an existing managed client instead of launching a duplicate.
- Closing a storefront is explicit and confirmed. SIGTERM, an 8-second stop
  budget and systemd cgroup cleanup apply. Failed/uncertain stops retain the
  reservation until a fresh stop succeeds. Startup recovers orphaned store units.
- Legacy `Status` remains the emulator game session; it never represents Steam.
  The additive `StorefrontStatus` reports id, generation, phase, Guide owner,
  detected Steam game and error. `StorefrontAction(action,id,generation)` supports
  launch/home/close. Home/close require the current generation (decimal string).
- `ForegroundStatus` reports library/storefront/game. A detected Steam game is
  `game` with its client identified separately by `StorefrontStatus`.
- Game windows are detected by an owned `steam_app_<nonzero id>` WM class or a
  nonzero `SteamAppId` in the owned window process environment. This must be
  qualified against real native and Proton games; games escaping the service
  cgroup or lacking these identifiers are not currently classified.
- Zaman never invokes emulator `ExitGame` on Steam. While a detected Steam game
  runs, the menu offers Resume, confirmed Close Steam, and system settings.
  Exit only the game inside Steam. Close Steam shuts down the managed client
  and its game together. Cancel leaves both running. Return to
  Library remains blocked during gameplay. Closing only the game inside Steam
  allows the client window to become primary again.
- This does not yet supervise games launched from Dukkan/Flatpak as independent
  sessions, persist installs beyond Dukkan UI exit, or add notifications.

## Source build (owner runs; nothing installed by the assistant)

Fetch into your existing clones without overwriting local edits. Prefer separate
worktrees for this candidate. Record the installed version and current branch.
Build sessiond and both development helpers together:

```bash
cargo test --locked --offline
cargo build --release --locked --offline
```

Use the sessiond helper as canonical. `zaman-menu/apply.py` recognizes both
published helper baselines and retains the snapshot's parallel identity reads;
it is unnecessary when using this sessiond candidate directly. If you use it,
run it before the build and rebuild the helpers.

Dukkan uses the existing CMake workflow from its README. Its only change is a
stable Wayland desktop/app identity. Use the existing Qt/SDL dependencies.
Do not upgrade or install packages as part of this candidate automatically.

## Configure executable paths

Close any manually launched Dukkan/Steam before the first managed launch. An
already-running external Steam client cannot be adopted into a new cgroup.
Check the actual executables:

```bash
command -v steam
ls -l "$HOME/projects/dukkan/build/dukkan"
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/zaman/storefronts.d"
```

Copy the two `.toml.example` files from `registry/storefronts.d/` to that
configuration directory as `dukkan.toml` and `steam.toml`, only if there is no
existing config. Edit their absolute argv paths to match your device. Dukkan's
example uses `/home/kadhem/projects/dukkan/build/dukkan`; Steam's uses
`/usr/bin/steam -gamepadui`. They are examples, not discovered device paths.
`argv` is passed directly to systemd, without shell parsing. Optional `env` and
`workdir` use the same validation as emulator commands.

Keep `native_guide = false` initially. After Steam overlay acceptance, set it
true in `steam.toml` and close/relaunch the managed Steam client. This passes the
controller through with InputPlumber NONE while Steam is active, so Steam receives
Guide. Manual Zaman menu opening still acquires ALL; closing restores the saved
mode. F12/your existing shortcut remains a Zaman escape route. Start+Select is
verified on this Q6A with the shortcut guard admitting `storefront`. Preserve
its launcher/project environment adapter. To revert delegation, set false and
close/relaunch Steam.

Deploy only after your build passes, using your existing sessiond installer and
resident menu setup. Ensure `ZAMAN_MENU_QML` points to the matching menu checkout
(or its default `$HOME/zaman-quickshell-prototype/qml/shell.qml`). The new helper
requires the additive StorefrontStatus API; update both repositories together.
The installer refuses to replace binaries while either store unit is active.

## Device acceptance

Run each case from Pegasus using only a controller, at 1080p and 1440p:

1. Guide > Storefronts > Dukkan. Verify `store-dukkan`, borderless fullscreen.
   Open/close Guide ten times. Check the Dukkan window stays fullscreen and
   returns to its prior focus. Pegasus must never tile beside it.
2. Home returns to Pegasus; reopening Dukkan retains its browsing state. Close
   storefront requests confirmation and returns to Pegasus after cleanup.
3. Repeat for Steam. Start a native game and a Proton game. Read
   `zamanctl storefront-status`; verify `game=true`, no emulator Exit Game action, confirmed Close Steam available, and that exiting inside Steam keeps Steam running/fullscreen.
4. Enable native Guide only after the overlay works. Check short presses,
   repeat presses/holds, Steam overlay close, F12 Zaman menu, and return to library.
5. While Guide is open in each storefront, unplug/reconnect the controller,
   restart InputPlumber, and disconnect while holding a direction. The page
   stays open, held navigation stops, and input recovers without a new menu.
6. Kill the storefront's main process, test an invalid executable config, and
   test a client exiting during startup/Guide presentation. Expect Home recovery,
   no orphan interception, a journal error for failures, and usable relaunch.
7. Return Home with a storefront running and launch an existing emulator game.
   Check normal Guide/exit/autosave and foreground restoration remain intact.
8. Rapidly select a launch/close action and press Guide. The UI must wait for
   helper-idle, dispatch once, reject stale generations and avoid focus races.

Diagnostics:

```bash
zamanctl status
zamanctl storefront-status
swaymsg -t get_tree
systemctl --user status zaman-store-dukkan.service zaman-store-steam.service
journalctl --user -u zaman-sessiond.service -n 100 --no-pager
```

CLI launch: `zamanctl storefront launch dukkan` or `... steam`.
Return/close: `zamanctl storefront home` or `... close` (menu must be hidden).
An accepted request is not proof the UI is ready; observe StorefrontStatus.

## Rollback

Close any games and managed storefronts before replacing binaries. If normal
close is unavailable, stop the two managed user units explicitly, then stop
sessiond and the resident renderer. Restore the installer's saved binaries and
the previous menu checkout/service path; rebuild the previous helper if needed.
Keep or remove only the new storefront config files you created. The daemon API
and helper must be rolled back together. Restart the previous services and verify
Pegasus, Guide, controller recovery, and emulator graceful exit.

## Tested Steam display setting

Keep Steam Settings > Display > Big Picture Mode > **Windowed ON**. This
resolved the Silksong rendering failure over repeated fresh managed sessions
and reboot on this device. Keep normal Silksong launch options. The failed
update-3 Pegasus-pause helper is rolled back and excluded from the checkpoint.
The low-level rendering cause remains unproven.

docs/potential-features.md.content:
# Potential features

These are proposals, not implemented features or installed changes.

## Steam controller shortcut reminder

Requested by Kadhem on 2026-10-13 after validating managed Steam and the
Start + Select route to Zaman's fallback menu.

- On a managed Steam foreground launch, show a short Zaman notification:
  **"Zaman menu: press Start + Select."**
- Explain that this shortcut opens Zaman's system menu while Guide belongs
  to Steam. Use controller button glyphs alongside the text where available.
- Show once per Steam session, after the client is visible. Returning from
  Guide or reopening the same background client should not repeat it.
- Use the existing notification/toast design. It must not take keyboard or
  controller focus, intercept inputs, pause the game, or require dismissal.
- Allow the reminder to be disabled. Keep it available in a future Controls
  reference/help page after the user disables the startup reminder.
- A notification is appropriate here; this is not a modal dialog.

Acceptance: cold Steam launch shows the hint once; Steam Guide and game
controls still work; Start + Select opens Zaman's menu; subsequent menu cycles
do not repeat the hint; a new Steam session may show it again unless disabled.

docs/sprint1-acceptance-20261014.md.content:
# Sprint 1 recovery acceptance — 2026-10-14

Owner-reported device results, Dragon Q6A; these are not container runtime tests.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Steam Windowed ON, normal Silksong options, fresh sessions and reboot | Pass |
| Start + Select opens Zaman menu in Steam | Pass |
| Close Steam -> Cancel leaves Silksong running | Pass |
| Confirm Close Steam closes client/game -> responsive Library | Pass |
| Emulator launch, Guide, normal exit -> Pegasus | Pass |
| Dukkan opens/closes normally through menu | Pass |
| Controller reconnect in game and menu | Pass |

This accepts the tested recovery round, not the entire original native/Proton,
resolution, abnormal-exit and race matrix. Fallout 4 and Another Crab's Treasure
never launch, including the prior Cage setup; compatibility investigation is
explicitly deferred. No working Windows/Proton-game acceptance is claimed.

Keep Steam Big Picture Windowed ON, the existing native ARM64 Steam wrapper and
native Guide choice. Update 3's Pegasus-pause helper remains rolled back. Steam
workspace routing, Close Steam generation validation, menu input restoration
before shutdown, and the Start+Select storefront guard form the working baseline.

The Start+Select reminder popup is recorded in potential-features.md and is not
implemented. Next work: independent installed-game sessions launched from Dukkan.

docs/sprint2-dukkan-games.md.content:
# Sprint 2: installed games launched from Dukkan

## Current source boundary

Dukkan has four curated identifiers, user Flatpak install/remove, ARM64 remote
availability checks, confirmation, and installed-state refresh. It has no game
launch method. Installed-game selection currently opens a removal confirmation.
Sessiond's existing Launch is ROM/emulator-oriented; StorefrontAction supervises
clients. A Flatpak game must not become a child that Close Dukkan can kill.

## First implementation slice

- Add a daemon-owned catalog/launch registry. Dukkan submits only the curated app
  ID; remote artwork/metadata cannot provide argv, flags, executable paths or env.
- Verify the exact user installation and aarch64 ref locally before launch.
  Resolve an explicit installed branch/ref, avoiding ambiguous app IDs.
- Add an additive installed-game API and CLI with request acknowledgment and
  session identity. Do not falsify ROM paths or alter the emulator Launch API.
- Start one managed game independently of zaman-store-dukkan.service; Dukkan
  remains alive in store-dukkan. Enforce a single active game across emulator,
  installed game and detected Steam game; serialize launch/stop and reject races.
- Place the game in a game workspace using verified ownership. Flatpak can create
  an app scope through its session helper; validate actual cgroups before relying
  on the launcher PID or inherited parent cgroup. Record exact Flatpak instance
  identity and use it for lifecycle cleanup if needed. Never stop all Flatpaks.
- Menu Resume and Exit Game target this game. Restore input before actions.
  Use a normal window close first; qualify a bounded forced-stop fallback.
  Do not inherit emulator save-state assumptions for native applications.
- Natural exit or confirmed Exit Game returns to responsive Library. Reopening
  Dukkan preserves its browsing state; closing Dukkan must not stop the game.
- Dukkan details show Play as the primary installed action, Remove separately
  with the existing confirmation. Busy state and launch errors prevent duplicate
  dispatch and provide a recoverable UI.

## Device qualification gate

Before finalizing lifecycle code, inspect one manually launched existing curated
user ARM64 Flatpak: exact installed ref, flatpak ps instance/PID, /proc cgroup,
Sway window pid/app_id/class, natural exit and normal window-close behavior.
This is a deliberate device qualification step, not an assumption that the
launcher owns the whole runtime. No dependency installation is required.

## Acceptance

1. Install an available curated ARM64 game with confirmation; refresh -> installed.
2. Select Play -> one foreground game; no tiling with Pegasus or Dukkan.
3. Guide -> Resume preserves input; reconnect works while menu/game is active.
4. Natural quit -> Library; reopen Dukkan -> browsing state retained.
5. Exit Game confirmation/cancel and graceful/forced cleanup affect only that game.
6. Missing app/architecture, failed launch, double Play and client close are safe.
7. Restart daemon -> no orphan game or stuck controller interception.
8. Retest accepted Steam/emulator/Dukkan recovery baseline.

Catalog expansion, background transaction service, Pegasus catalog export and
notification popup are separate work after this launch/lifecycle slice.

tools/test-sprint1-checkpoint.py.content:
"""Exercise real Git checkpoints without the owner's device or network."""
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
WORKSPACE = ROOT.parent
SCRIPT = ROOT / 'tools/checkpoint-sprint1.py'
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('checkpoint', SCRIPT)
mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(mod)


class CheckpointTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.manifest = json.loads(SCRIPT.with_name('sprint1-checkpoint.json').read_text())
        self.repos = {}
        for name in self.manifest['paths']:
            target = self.root / name
            shutil.copytree(WORKSPACE / name, target,
                            ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('.git', 'target', 'build', '__pycache__'))
            subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q', '-b', 'sprint1/storefronts', str(target)], check=True)
            mod.git(target, 'config', 'user.name', 'Test')
            mod.git(target, 'config', 'user.email', 'test@example.com')
            mod.git(target, 'add', '.')
            mod.git(target, 'commit', '-qm', 'Fixture baseline')
            self.repos[name] = target

    def test_checkpoint_commits_only_allowlisted_sources_and_keeps_backups(self):
        repo = self.repos['zaman-sessiond']
        original = repo / 'tools/steam-foreground-handoff.py'
        mod.git(repo, 'rm', '--cached', str(original.relative_to(repo)))
        mod.git(repo, 'commit', '-qm', 'Untrack failed experiment')
        (repo / 'unrelated.txt').write_text('private untracked experiment')
        (repo / 'README.md').write_text((repo / 'README.md').read_text() + '\nCheckpoint fixture change\n')
        mod.preflight(self.repos, self.manifest)
        backup = self.root / 'backup'
        mod.checkpoint(self.repos, self.manifest, backup, {}, SCRIPT)
        refs = mod.commit_and_tag(self.repos, 'snapshot/test-accepted')
        self.assertEqual(set(refs), set(self.repos))
        names = mod.git(repo, 'ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', 'HEAD').decode().splitlines()
        self.assertNotIn('unrelated.txt', names)
        self.assertNotIn('tools/steam-foreground-handoff.py', names)
        self.assertTrue(original.exists())
        self.assertTrue((backup / 'zaman-sessiond/before.bundle').is_file())
        self.assertTrue((backup / 'zaman-sessiond/files/README.md').is_file())
        self.assertIn(b'Checkpoint fixture change', (backup / 'zaman-sessiond/working.patch').read_bytes())
        mod.preflight(self.repos, self.manifest)
        # A repeated source checkpoint has no new staged changes or empty commit.
        mod.checkpoint(self.repos, self.manifest, self.root / 'repeat-backup', {}, SCRIPT)
        repeated = mod.commit_and_tag(self.repos, 'snapshot/test-repeat')
        self.assertEqual(refs, repeated)
        values = json.loads((self.repos['zaman-menu'] / 'SHA256.json').read_text())
        for relative, expected in values.items():
            self.assertEqual(mod.digest((self.repos['zaman-menu'] / relative).read_bytes()), expected)

    def test_unknown_staged_file_is_refused(self):
        repo = self.repos['dukkan']
        (repo / 'unrelated.txt').write_text('unrelated')
        mod.git(repo, 'add', 'unrelated.txt')
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, 'unrelated staged'):
            mod.preflight(self.repos, self.manifest)

    def test_changed_tested_source_is_refused(self):
        (self.repos['zaman-menu'] / 'qml/shell.qml').write_text('different runtime')
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, 'tested recovery'):
            mod.preflight(self.repos, self.manifest)

    def test_unknown_document_edit_is_refused(self):
        (self.repos['dukkan'] / 'docs/SESSION-INTEGRATION.md').write_text('owner edit')
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, 'unexpected document edit'):
            mod.preflight(self.repos, self.manifest)

    def test_symlink_is_refused(self):
        path = self.repos['zaman-menu'] / 'qml/shell.qml'
        path.unlink()
        path.symlink_to(WORKSPACE / 'zaman-menu/qml/shell.qml')
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, 'Unsafe path'):
            mod.preflight(self.repos, self.manifest)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

docs/sprint1-storefronts.md.content:
# Sprint 1 menu candidate

Use with `citrineio/zaman-sessiond` branch `sprint1/storefronts`, based on the
published `snapshot/quickshell-20261012`, and the matching Dukkan branch.
See the daemon's `docs/sprint1-storefronts.md` for setup, acceptance and rollback.

Adds equal Dukkan/Steam rows under Storefronts on Home. The Guide menu adapts
Resume, Return to library and Close storefront to the managed application.
Closing a storefront requires confirmation. Detected Steam games do not expose
Zaman's emulator Exit Game; exit inside Steam to preserve its client.

A storefront action first hides the layer and waits for the resident helper's
idle acknowledgement, proving input/focus restoration. Only then does the
one-shot session bridge pin a unique sessiond bus owner and request the action.
Duplicate requests and late readiness cannot overlap the handoff. Generations
remain decimal strings so Qt/JavaScript cannot truncate them. Failure reopens the
menu with an error. Helper failure cancels the queued action.

The helper accepts managed storefront context and includes its id/generation in
ready. Both repos ship the same helper, including the published sessiond snapshot's
concurrent identity reads. Rebuild it; a QML-only update is insufficient. No
production install or package installation was performed by the assistant.

Validation: existing and new Python bridge tests, actual QML-function JS tests,
shell syntax and bundle checks. QML rendering, Rust compilation, controller
hardware and Steam overlay acceptance remain with the device owner.

## Accepted recovery update (2026-10-14)

Kadhem verified Close Steam -> Cancel preserves the game, confirmation closes
Steam and Silksong and returns to responsive Library, emulator Guide/normal
exit/Pegasus return, Dukkan menu open/close, and controller reconnect in game
and menu. Start+Select works during Steam sessions. Close Steam is available
during a detected managed Steam game; it explicitly closes both game and client.
Keep the shortcut's device launcher/project adapter and storefront guard.

docs/SESSION-INTEGRATION.md.content:
# Zaman managed storefront integration

Sprint 1 adds `com.kawnelectro.Dukkan` as a stable desktop/Wayland app identity.
The existing fullscreen QML window and input gating are unchanged.

Use `zamanctl storefront launch dukkan` or Zaman Guide > Storefronts > Dukkan
with the matching `sprint1/storefronts` branches of zaman-sessiond/zaman-menu.
Configure the built executable's absolute path in
`~/.config/zaman/storefronts.d/dukkan.toml`. Close a manually launched copy first.

Sessiond supervises the client in its own systemd cgroup/Sway workspace; Home
preserves it, Resume restores it, and Close storefront terminates it explicitly.
This change does not move installations into a background service or supervise
Flatpak-launched games as independent Zaman sessions. Those remain follow-on work.

Kadhem built and activated the candidate on Q6A and verified Dukkan opens and
closes normally through the Zaman menu (2026-10-14). Emulator and Steam recovery
regressions also passed. Installing/removing games is not claimed accepted by
that result; installed-game launch remains unimplemented.

Local Python checks alone do not establish Qt compilation/runtime behavior.
